chunks: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz al-Qurashi al-Kufi narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Razi, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him) say: Whoever is not enabled to visit us, let him visit the righteous of our followers; the reward of our visitation is recorded for him. And whoever is not able to connect with us, let him connect with the righteous of our followers; the reward of our connection is recorded for him.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ: Abu al-Hasan the First (Imam Musa al-Kazim)
key_terms.يُكْتَبْ لَهُ: It is recorded for him (as a reward)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the righteous followers of the Imams if one cannot visit the Imams directly?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the theological principle of 'vicarious ziyarah,' where the righteous followers (al-mawali) serve as a spiritual extension of the Imam, allowing the faithful to maintain a tangible connection to the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the communal network of leadership, where loyalty to the Imams is practically manifested through service to their devoted followers, ensuring that physical distance does not sever spiritual reward.
